title: Psalm 82: God Judges the Judges
summary: God takes his place in a heavenly assembly and puts the powers who rule the world on trial. He charges them with judging unjustly and favoring the wicked, commands them to defend the weak, the fatherless, and the oppressed, and sentences them to die like mortals. The psalmist then calls on God himself to rise and judge the earth, because all the nations belong to him.
line: God puts the powers that rule the world on trial for judging unjustly, commands them to defend the weak and the fatherless, and the psalmist asks God himself to judge the earth.
guide: Anyone with power over others, a parent, a boss, a teacher, a pastor, will answer to God for how the weak were treated; ask who near you has no one to speak for them. When the courts and the powerful fail, pray verse 8, which hands justice to the one judge who will not fail.

stanzas.title: God takes his seat in the divine assembly
The charge: unjust judgment and neglect of the weak
The accused walk in darkness and the earth shakes
The sentence: the gods will die like mortals
The prayer: rise, O God, and judge the earth

verses.t: A Psalm of Asaph. God presides in the divine assembly; He renders judgment among the gods:
“How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.
Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.
They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall.”
Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.
